subject.title: [Feature]: Network Access Control (allowedDomains / denyDomains) — Egress Firewall

question: What public egress security boundary should OpenClaw expose for domain allow/deny controls across web_fetch, web_search, providers, browser, and proxy-routed fetches?
rationale: The requested config would become an operator-trusted network exfiltration boundary, and the open related PRs represent different security and ownership models that automation should not choose.

options.title: Define Shared Egress Policy
options.body: Set a cross-tool contract for names, deny precedence, redirects, cache/provider fallback, search providers, browser, and proxy routing before implementation lands.

options.title: Sponsor Scoped web_fetch First
options.body: Accept the narrow web_fetch hostname-allowlist path as an interim contract and keep denyDomains plus web_search/browser/proxy coverage as explicit follow-up work.

options.title: Use Managed Proxy Boundary
options.body: Route application-owned egress policy through proxy.enabled and external operator policy instead of adding local domain firewall knobs to web tools.

recommendation.title: Define Shared Egress Policy
recommendation.body: Set a cross-tool contract for names, deny precedence, redirects, cache/provider fallback, search providers, browser, and proxy routing before implementation lands.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter has the strongest historical ownership across the existing web_fetch, guarded-fetch, and SSRF policy boundary and is the best available owner for the product/security contract choice.
